biography.plain_text: John von Neumann was an Austrian-born car importer who helped establish Porsche in California. He founded Competition Motors in North Hollywood and later distributed Porsche and Volkswagen vehicles across the western United States. An avid racer, he used motorsport and his Hollywood connections to introduce the unfamiliar sports cars to American customers.

long_biography.plain_text:
A Porsche 356 bought in New York became a calling card for John von Neumann's California car business. He had opened Competition Motors in North Hollywood in 1948, after wartime Army service and a job selling imported cars. He raced and promoted the machines himself, helping build a sports-car audience on the West Coast. His showroom drew drivers and Hollywood customers as Porsche's reputation grew.

Von Neumann expanded from retail into the distribution of Porsche and Volkswagen cars through a western dealer network. The Volkswagen factory eventually acquired his distributorship, a major realization of the business he had built. Born in Vienna, he had emigrated with his family before settling in America. He died in 2003, leaving a distinct legacy in early American sports-car racing as well as automotive retail.
